chunks: Ahmad, from Ali, from Sayf, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, that he asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
The keeping (of the intention) in the mind is more beloved to me, therefore exclaim Talbiyya and do not specify.

key_terms.الْإِضْمَارُ: Keeping the intention or recitation in the heart/mind silently
key_terms.فَلَبِّ: Exclaim or call out (imperative form related to Talbiyya)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for reciting the Talbiyya during Ihram according to Imam Musa al-Kazim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) establishes the preference for *idmar* (silent intention) over vocal recitation for the Talbiyya, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the internal state of devotion (*khushu*) as the core of ritual acts. This ruling distinguishes the Imam's guidance from other schools that prioritize audible recitation, highlighting the theological weight placed on the heart's presence during the initial call to God. The instruction to 'Talbi' without verbal specification underscores that the essence of the pilgrimage lies in the spiritual response rather than mere phonetic performance.
